title: Sheeva Dragonsister
type: Zarathian operative, honored lady, and painter
dek: A soldierly intelligence operative whose public service, painting, and growing trust in Eugene preserve different parts of her life after war.

facts.Public accomplishment: Discovery of captives being fed to dragons

sources: Zarathis_Dragonsisters_NPC_Master.md — supplied 5 October 2026; quest-RP parts 024, 026, 030 and explicit evidence distinctions
body:
Sheeva is one of the Dragonsisters, the three Dragonborn agents whose long infiltration helped Zarathis understand and defeat the draconic cultists. Captain Zythienne specifically credits her with discovering the feeding of enslaved captives to dragons.

A public hero with a history beneath the mask

At the July 2025 ceremony Sheeva stands proudly, and later observation identifies her as the sisters’ social leader. Her role in the mission remains broader than one named discovery, but the recovered record does not give her a formal rank over Kaiya and Minyah.

In the July interaction that leads Eugene toward her, the paired sister is described as soldierly, masked, apparently concealing a battle scar, and letting the others speak. Later dialogue resolves that pairing onto Sheeva. Kaiya is separately described as normally masked, so the mask is not an exclusive means of identifying Sheeva.

The origin of the scar and her exact experiences undercover remain unrecovered. Her presentation supports a history touched by violence without supplying a diagnosis or an invented account of how she was injured.

15 July: Eugene notices the reserve

Eugene first notices discomfort in the crowd because he recognizes something familiar in it. Later that evening he addresses Sheeva by name, apologizes when an urgent discussion pulls him away, and returns to the leap they had planned together. The record establishes his return to her, without recovering the full details of the leap.

19 August: painting and mutual interest

At their reunion Eugene asks Lady Sheeva to dance. She says she missed him and responds affectionately. She takes interest in his Shadow Roads research and invites a future walk together. His intellectual life is part of what she wants to know.

Sheeva has been painting because she has heard it can heal the heart and mind. She shows him a work centered on Eugene, whom she calls the thing occupying her thoughts. The scene joins her own attempt to recover after the war with an emerging relationship; it does not establish that Eugene cured her distress.

By August her interest is openly reciprocal. She wants to leave with her gallant man, while Kaiya approves of Eugene’s humility and the dignity with which he treats her sister.

5 December: familiarity and trusted company

Sheeva and Eugene greet each other warmly after another absence. Before treating the evening as theirs alone, he insists they first pay respects and offer condolences in her home. She calls this honorable; he also declines credit for an idea that was not his own.

Later distress leads Sheeva to ask for his company rather than being alone. This shows vulnerability and trust alongside the brave, teasing public figure. The biography preserves the emotional significance without making the relationship her entire identity.

The relationship and the open record

Repeated reunions, affection, explicit flirtation, the painting, and Kaiya’s approval establish a meaningful mutual attachment. Marriage, engagement, exclusivity, children, formal vows, relocation, or abandonment of either person’s other obligations are not established.

Her five-year service predates Eugene. Its exact methods, her ancestry, age, scar’s origin, later artistic work, and eventual fate remain open. Sheeva’s history includes intelligence, national recognition, recovery, and affection without allowing one part to replace the others.
